title: Cut a seized padlock off a storage-cage gate with a two-handed bolt cutter, closing both handles together on one shackle leg
instruction: Cut the padlock off the cage gate.
context: Cutting off a padlock whose key is lost or whose body has seized is routine work for building and facilities maintenance workers and locksmiths: storage cages, lockers, gates and containers. A bolt cutter takes both hands, one on each long handle. The open jaws have to be set square across one shackle leg, as deep in the jaws as it will go, and the two handles closed together, so the head stays where it is: closing one handle against a held one swings the head, drags and twists the lock and lets the blades slip off the round leg. Once the leg is cut the cutter is laid down.
setup: Bench top is z = 0; x away from the arm bases, y to the left. A run of steel-mesh storage-cage wall stands on the bench along x (x 0.38 to 0.74) with its face toward -y at y 0.04: a 40 mm square-tube fixed post centred at x 0.52 and the gate's latch stile beside it at x 0.472, both 400 mm tall, 6 mm mesh on a 50 mm grid either side. A hasp's staple on the post holds its eye 40 mm proud of it (y 0.0) at 200 mm height. Through it hangs a 40 mm brass padlock (body 40 x 20 x 36 mm, 220 g) on a 6 mm plain-steel shackle, legs 28 mm apart (x 0.506 and 0.534), 30 mm of each showing between the bow and the body. A steel tool case (230 x 190 x 90 mm, centred x 0.515, y -0.06) stands in front of the wall; on it, beside the lock, lies a 14 in (355 mm) bolt cutter, 0.75 kg, shut, pivot at x 0.56, y -0.04, jaws toward +x, its 28 mm rubber grips (110 mm long, middles 260 mm behind the pivot, at about x 0.31, y -0.10 and 0.02) overhanging the case's near edge. Its handles open up to 26 degrees, the blades then 13.6 mm apart at their cutting point 30 mm ahead of the pivot.
scoring: 0.25: a shackle leg between the jaws at their cutting point (16 to 43 mm ahead of the pivot), square to them (within 20 degrees). 0.5: the leg cut through. 0.75: also the lock not dragged: until the cut it never moved more than 10 mm from where it hung (the head held still while the two handles closed together; real trial: filmed against a scale behind the lock, or a dial gauge on its body). 1.0: also the cutter laid back down on the case (both bodies within 15 mm of their resting height), let go of (no closed hand within 6 cm of either grip) and both hands at least 10 cm from the lock, held 1 s.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. The bolt cutter is two rigid bodies on a single pivot (a stand-in for the compound linkage, 0.115 mm of jaw per mm of grip travel). Shearing is a rule: a leg square between the blades at their cutting point with them closed down onto it (gap within 0.5 mm of the 6 mm leg) for 0.25 s is cut, and its 14 mm cut zone is then no longer collided with and drawn gone, so the blades close through; no cutting force (a real cutter needs about 400 N at the grips), no blade wear. The padlock swings on the staple's eye (a hinge about the eye; the eye is drawn only); the staple and hasp do not bend. The YAM's parallel fingers clamp each grip top and bottom; a hand's wrap is not modelled.
